summary: Deming Mountain lookout, removed in 1985; its cab is on display outdoors at the Forks Timber Museum. Sources disagree on which cab and tower reached Forks.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says Forks Museum; the Forest Fire Lookout Association list and WillhiteWeb say Forks Timber Museum. The story uses Forks Timber Museum.

WillhiteWeb says the cab was built in 1965 and reached Forks in 1985. The Forest Lookouts page links an 8-by-8 cab to the 1947 steel tower. The register does not say which cab went to Forks. The story reports both and does not settle it.
The register gives an 80-foot pole tower first used in 1929. The Forest Lookouts page describes the earlier structure as a small tower of native materials. The story reports the disagreement.
The register gives 1965 for the 40-foot wooden DNR tower; the Forest Lookouts page gives 1964-66. The two agree within the range; the story uses 1965 and notes the wider span.

sources.title: Deming Lookout at Forks Timber Museum

notes_for_editor: Reads: register, firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts page (two passes on the cached page), FFA Washington list, WillhiteWeb Forks page, museum exhibits page; one WebSearch. A WebSearch hit on WillhiteWeb's Deming page (sumas_mountain_271) was not read and is not used. Record check: the Forks record's county (Clallam), coordinates and standing status match the FFA list. The register's Date Registered value did not appear in the cached text, so the March 26, 2012 date in the us-wa-deming record is unverified. The record has no year for the relocation; the story adds 1985 for the cab move. Height is left out: the 75-foot and 40-foot figures belong to different towers, and the source tower for the cab is disputed. Access 'public' rests on the museum display page; the museum invites visits, but no hours or climbing rules were found. Story is about the lookout, so the original Deming site is covered only as the place the tower came from.
